info.title: BWH eSign native API
info.summary: Prepare, send, track, and retrieve signed PDF agreements.
info.description:
The native HTTP surface of BWH eSign. It and the Firma-compatible facade under `/functions/v1/signing-request-api` call the same domain services; signing rules live in the state machine and never in an HTTP controller.

**Tenancy.** There is no workspace parameter anywhere in this API. The credential presented in `Authorization` belongs to exactly one workspace, and that is the tenant for every lookup. An id belonging to another workspace answers `404`, identical to an id that does not exist, so a caller cannot probe for the existence of another tenant's records.

**Errors.** Every failure is `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Switch on `code`; the message is for a human reading a log. Codes are stable and renaming one is a breaking change.

**Honest language.** Humans provide electronic signatures and assent; the service seals the finished PDF under its own certificate. Nothing here is a per-signer certificate, and no assurance level beyond the PAdES baselines named in `assurance_level` is claimed.

post.description:
From a published `template_version_id`, or from a `document_id` plus the `field_schema` to place on it. Exactly one of the two; sending both is a `422` rather than one silently winning.

The envelope copies its source. A template edited afterwards can never change an agreement already out for signature.

`recipients[].id` is the **schema** recipient id (`buyer`, `seller`) — the handle fields use to find their owner. The name and email given here are written into the copied schema before anything is persisted, so the envelope, its recipients, and their identity snapshots agree from the first row. An id the schema does not declare is `422 unknown_recipient`, never ignored.

`expires_in_hours` is tri-state: omit it for the seven-day default, give a number of hours, or send `null` for an envelope that never expires.

Creation does not send. The envelope is a draft until `POST /envelopes/{envelope}/send`.

patch.description:
Drafts only. Two things are correctable before an envelope goes out: what the sender prefilled, and who the parties are. A non-draft envelope is `409 illegal_transition` — after send an invitation has been addressed and material content is on its way to being signed, so a correction is a new envelope with renewed signatures.

Prefills go through the state machine as the sender, which is what decides whether a given field is the sender's to write: a read-only field is, a signature never is, and a service-supplied field is nobody's. The copied field schema itself is immutable and is never touched.

post.description:
Legal from `draft` only; sending twice is `409 illegal_transition`.

This is the last cheap moment: after it, correcting material content means a new envelope. The gate is strict and reports **every** problem at once under `details.problems`, so a caller fixing an envelope sees the whole list rather than discovering the next problem after fixing the previous one.

A requested assurance level the deployment cannot actually meet is a problem here, never a silent downgrade.

post.description:
Legal from `draft`, `sent`, and `in_progress`. Not from `finalizing`: everybody has signed by then and an artifact is being produced from their acceptances. Not from a terminal state either — cancelling a completed envelope is `409`.

Expiry is a fact about the clock, not a button. An envelope a sender wants to stop early is cancelled, which records a reason and says honestly what happened.

get.description:
Every field of the schema, in schema order, with the value it currently holds. Readable at any point in the lifecycle, not only after completion.

`signature` and `initials` fields are **described** rather than dumped: `signature` carries the media type, the digest of the image bytes, and their length, and `value` is null. That is the default because an image returned unasked ends up in the caller's request logs, proxy caches, and error reports. `?include=images` adds `signature.data`, the captured value verbatim.

`signing_date` is supplied by the service from the owning recipient's attestation and is never submitted by anyone.

get.description: Two different refusals, and they mean different things. An envelope that has not completed is `409 not_completed` — a statement about the envelope. A **completed** envelope with no published artifact is `501 unsupported` — a statement about this build, where finalization produced nothing for it. Neither is ever a `200` with an empty list, which would tell a caller an agreement has no PDF.

get.summary: The whole evidence export as one zip.
get.description: Everything docs/HANDOFF.md section 8 requires in an export, in one archive: the original upload, the reviewed revision, the executed PDF, the machine-readable evidence document, the human-readable completion report, the seal certificate chain, the validation report, and a `manifest.json` giving each file its SHA-256 and a sentence saying what that digest covers. The manifest is deliberately unsigned — a signature by this service over its own inventory would add no independent assurance, and the seal that matters is inside the executed PDF. Streamed through the application; nothing is presigned.

post.description:
The response carries `secret` **once**. Only ciphertext is stored and there is no route that returns it again: a lost secret is rotated, never recovered.

The URL is validated against the deployment's outbound destination policy at creation rather than at delivery time, so a destination that would be refused is a `422` on this call instead of a silent queue failure later.

Omit `event_filter` (or send `null`) for every event.

serviceCredential.description:
A service credential in `Authorization`. Both syntaxes authenticate and are equivalent:

    Authorization: esk_<prefix>_<secret>
    Authorization: Bearer esk_<prefix>_<secret>

The raw form is accepted because the API this application is compatible with sends its key with no scheme. Native callers should use `Bearer`. Credentials are issued, rotated, and revoked from the console (`docs/operations/service-credentials.md`); there is no self-service route and no way to read a secret back.

Error.description: Every failure on this API. Switch on `error.code`; the message is for a human reading a log.

code.description: Stable machine code. Renaming one is a breaking change.

details.description: Present when there is something structured to say: `fields` for validation, `problems` for a send gate, `required_scope` for a 403.

PageMeta.description: There is no total and no page number. Counting a tenant's rows on every request buys a number that is stale before it renders, and there are no pages to number in a keyset scheme.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page. Null means this is the last.

prefix.description: The public half of the key. Safe to quote in a ticket; it is what every console command identifies a credential by.

last_used_at.description: Written at most once a minute, so a read-only request is not also a write.

scopes.description: Exactly what was granted. Nothing is implied: `envelopes:write` does not grant `envelopes:read`.

retired_at.description: Set on a template that should no longer be chosen for new work. Still listed, so a stored id can be told from a deleted one.

current_version.description: The published version a caller gets by picking this template. Null until the first publish; a template with only drafts is deliberately not sendable.

versions.description: Every published version, oldest first. Drafts never appear.

sha256.description: The digest of the PDF this version will copy.

recipients.description: The roles to be addressed. Each entry's `id` is the `recipients[].id` `POST /envelopes` expects.

template_version_id.description: A published version id from the template catalogue.

document_id.description: A document with a review revision. Requires `field_schema`.

field_schema.description: A native field schema 1.0 document. Refused with `template_version_id`, which already carries one.

title.description: Defaults to the template's name, or the document's title.

assurance_level.description: An unrecognised value is an error, never a silent downgrade.

signing_mode.description: `parallel` requires a single-stage signing order; a multi-stage schema in parallel mode is refused rather than having its order quietly ignored.

expires_in_hours.description: Omit for the seven-day default; `null` for an envelope that never expires.

values.description: Sender prefills, schema field id to value. A signature is never the sender's to supply.

id.description: The **schema** recipient id, not the recipient's own public id. An id the schema does not declare is `422 unknown_recipient`.

values.description: Sender prefills to write or correct.

reason.description: Recorded on the envelope and in the cancellation event. Refused if too long rather than truncated: half a reason is a misleading reason.

state.description: `finalizing` is not `completed`: completion is asserted only once a validated final PDF is durably stored and retrievable. `finalization_failed` is visibly failed and retryable, never quietly complete.

version.description: The envelope's compare-and-swap token, not a document version. It moves on every transition.

source_template_version_id.description: Provenance only. The envelope copied the version and never dereferences it again.

document_sha256.description: What every attestation binds. Published so a caller can prove which document this envelope is.

content_frozen_at.description: When material content stopped being editable: the first acceptance, or send in parallel mode. After it, a prefill correction is refused rather than applied.

omitted_anchor_fields.description: Fields the source declared that were deliberately not placed, because their anchor declared that its text may legitimately be absent from this document and it was. Empty for almost every envelope. Written once, when the envelope is sent; an anchor that could not be resolved is a refused send, not an entry here. See docs/preparation/anchors.md.

id.description: This party's own public id, as named in event payloads.

schema_recipient_id.description: The handle the field schema uses. Fields find their owner by this, never by signing order and never by email.

order_index.description: Signing stage, from 1. In sequential mode a recipient stays `pending` until the stage before theirs finishes.

invited_at.description: When the invitation was actually written to this party. A delivery fact, not signing state: nothing in the state machine reads it, and a recipient's eligibility never depends on whether their mail was sent.

last_reminded_at.description: When they were last nudged. Null means never reminded, which is a different fact from reminded long ago.

recipient_id.description: The schema recipient who owns this field.

read_only.description: Read-only to the recipient. The sender may still prefill it — that is what read-only means here.

source.description: `service` is only `signing_date`, derived from the owning recipient's attestation.

value.description: The value, or null for a field nobody has completed. Always null for `signature` and `initials`, which are described under `signature` instead.

SignatureValue.description: A description of a captured mark. Bytes appear only when the request asked for them with `?include=images`.

type.description: The captured media type, or `application/octet-stream` for an opaque reference.

sha256.description: Digest of the decoded image bytes, so it is comparable with anything else that hashed the same image.

data.description: The captured value verbatim. Present only with `?include=images`.

id.description: The event identity a webhook receiver deduplicates on. The same id appears in the delivered body.

event.description: Names from the compatibility profile are reproduced verbatim; anything of ours is prefixed `esign.`.

occurred_at.description: When the transition happened, not when this row was read.

payload.description: The event's data object, exactly as recorded. Never rebuilt from current state.

download.description: A path on this API. Never a storage URL: bytes stream through the application on every driver.

event_filter.description: Omit or null for every event. An empty array is refused: it describes an endpoint that wants nothing, which is a disabled endpoint spelled confusingly.

enabled.description: `true` re-enables and clears the failure streak; `false` pauses deliveries.

grace_hours.description: How long the previous secret keeps verifying. `0` cuts over immediately.

consecutive_failures.description: An endpoint auto-disables after a run of failed deliveries.

secret_previous_expires_at.description: End of a rotation's overlap window, during which both secrets sign every attempt.

secret.description: Shown exactly once. Only ciphertext is stored and there is no route that returns it again.
